Released 2026-11-08 · [downloads and checksums on GitHub](https://github.com/BuenGenio/backdown-releases/releases/tag/v1.0.0-beta.8) · [Download page](/download/)
The eighth beta of BackDown 1.0: the date and place tags from beta.6 come to the app — an offline map of where your photos were taken, search by place, and tagging in bulk, in a new **Places** view — and `backdown tag find` finds them from the command line. It also carries beta.7's seconds-fast search by name across every machine.

## Install

| Platform | Installer | Command line |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x86-64 | `backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.8_amd64.deb` (Debian, Ubuntu) or `.AppImage` | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.8-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (static) |
| Linux ARM64 | `backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.8_arm64.deb` or `.AppImage` | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.8-linux-arm64.tar.gz` (static) |
| macOS (Apple silicon + Intel) | `BackDown-1.0.0-beta.8.dmg` | `backdown-v1.0.0-beta.8-macos-universal.tar.gz` |

Windows builds are paused for this beta while the port is finished; follow it at [https://github.com/BuenGenio/BackDown/issues/94](https://github.com/BuenGenio/BackDown/issues/94).

**This release is signed.** `SHA256SUMS.txt.sig` is an Ed25519 signature of `SHA256SUMS.txt` by BackDown's release key, and `backdown update` checks it before installing anything. To check by hand, see [Air-gapped computers](https://backdown.io/docs/guides/air-gapped/).

The installers and apps themselves still aren't signed by Apple. On macOS, right-click the app and choose Open the first time (for the command-line binary: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine backdown`).

## What's new since beta.6

### Find your photos by place — now in the app

beta.6 taught BackDown to read a photo's date and GPS position and turn the position into a country, a region, a city and the nearest airport, all offline (`tag exif`, `tag geo`). beta.8 brings that to the browser and the app, and makes it something you search.

- A new **Places** view: a search box that suggests places, tags and years; an **offline map** drawn from the place data built into BackDown — no tiles, nothing fetched — with your photos clustered on it and the search circle drawn; tag counts to narrow by; and a grid grouped by distance or month where you can **tag, untag, or set keep/drop/reviewed in bulk**.
- Reading a drive's photos is now a stoppable background job you watch in Places and Activity; each photo is read once, and reading a drive again only reads what's new.
- Rename, merge or delete your own tags from **All tags**.

### Find them from the command line

- **`backdown tag find`**: everything within a distance of an airport, a town or a position (`--near HKG`, `--near "Paris, Texas"`, `--near 22.31,113.91`), filtered by `--tag` and a `--from`/`--to` date range, newest or nearest first — with `--paths` and `--json` for scripts.
- **`backdown tag exif`** now takes folders, not just single files, and `--geo` names the country, city and airport in the same pass:

```sh
backdown tag exif /media/photos --geo
```

### Search answers in seconds, across every machine

Carried over from beta.7, which was never released on its own: a name index finds matches in a fraction of a second however big the index, and the search box's **Everywhere** covers your other machines too — this computer's matches first, then each machine's. After upgrading, the service builds the index once as its own job (about 8 minutes for 27 million files); search works as before until it's done.

## Known limitations

- Reverse-geocoding is to the nearest populated place of 1,000+ people; a photo far from any town takes the nearest one, with lower confidence. The named-place and airport matches are within a set distance.
- The name index takes some room: on 8.5 million distinct names, about 1.2 GB.
- Searching another machine at its fastest needs beta.8 there too.
- The installers aren't signed or notarised by Apple.
- Windows builds are paused this beta while the port is finished (#94); Linux and macOS are unaffected.
- Pro, Team and Forensic features are free during the beta; pricing may change before 1.0.

Documentation: https://backdown.io/docs/. Provided as-is, without warranty, for evaluation.
